brief: Digital assets rallied sharply in August 2026: bitcoin ran from the low $60,000s to above $80,000, up 25.37% on the month; ether returned 32.90%; solana returned 42.30%. Three forces combined. Rising US debt, now over $40 trillion, and Treasury Secretary Bessent's expanded long-dated Treasury buybacks pushed yields and the dollar lower, reviving a debasement narrative that frames bitcoin as digital gold. An August hack of Coinkite's Coldcard hardware wallets, roughly $150 million in bitcoin stolen, pushed investors toward custodied spot ETPs, lifting US bitcoin ETP inflows to a four-month high. A record short squeeze on August 19-20 liquidated over $1 billion of bitcoin shorts in an hour and $3 billion across crypto in 24 hours, fueling a 20%+ weekly bitcoin surge, while open interest stayed subdued, implying short covering rather than new leverage. Regulatory catalysts remain pending: the SEC proposed a crypto asset framework on August 18, still requiring public comment and a Commission vote, while the CLARITY Act faces a September 15 Senate cloture vote that Galaxy Research gives only 10% odds of becoming law in 2026. Invesco's authors call the risk skewed to the upside, flagging bitcoin's 50-week moving average, near $81,100, as the level that historically marks a durable turn.
